title: figma: migrate design/manifest capture to read-only canonical Figma file + amend ADR-0019
description:
The design manifest cites node ids from a COPY of the designer's file, and REST is dead, so citations rot silently. See design/manifest/PROVENANCE.md for the full statement.

Current state (verified under resonance-80bf):
- FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN returns 403. Every REST-backed tool is unavailable: figma_get_file_data, figma_get_file_versions, figma_get_file_at_version, download_assets, get_screenshot, get_metadata. Figma version ids are therefore NOT obtainable, so captures cannot be version-pinned.
- The only working read path is the Desktop Bridge plugin (figma_execute / figma_capture_screenshot) against whatever file the plugin has open.

Target state:

2. Refresh FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN so REST version-pinning works again.
3. Version-pin every capture (record the Figma version id alongside the content hash).

5. Demote 'Resonance (Copy)' to a cache; re-verify or re-capture screens 01-12 against canonical and drop the copy-derived flag.

title: infra: no-mistakes v1.40.3 custody deadlock — rebase writes objects to gate bare repo without advancing the branch ref
description:
Hit during Slice A step 3 (resonance-663d), no-mistakes v1.40.3 (d873960).

SYMPTOM: the pipeline's test step died on 'API Error: Connection closed mid-response' (a transport failure, not a test failure). Its rebase step had already replayed the branch commits onto a freshly-merged origin/main and written the resulting objects into the gate bare repo (~/.no-mistakes/repos/<id>.git), but never advanced the gate BRANCH REF to them. That wedges the two recovery paths against each other:
  - 'no-mistakes axi sync --recover' refuses with code 'blocked_recover_gate_diverged' (gate branch != preserved head)
  - 'no-mistakes axi run' refuses with next_action code 'recover_custody'
'--keep-local' does not bypass it; 'axi abort' is a no-op because the run is already terminal. There is no documented forward path.

WORKAROUND USED (needs review — it reaches into tool internals): verify the preserved commit is exclusively your own replayed work by confirming its tree equals your locally-rebased HEAD^{tree}, then complete the half-finished preservation with a compare-and-swap 'git update-ref' in the gate bare repo so it fails loudly if the ref moved. 'axi sync --recover --keep-local' then returns 'custody_returned' and a fresh run goes green. The gate was NOT bypassed and nothing was force-pushed.

WANTED: a supported recovery command for this state so agents never touch the gate's internal repo. v1.41.2 is available and may already fix it — the update was deliberately deferred during the fan-out because concurrent crewmates share the binary.

RELATED: resonance-3e21 (the older v1.31.2 'no previous run for branch' bug) is CLOSED — confirmed stale, v1.40.3 gates fresh treehouse branches cleanly. This is a different failure mode in the same custody machinery. Details also in the 'testing' mulch domain.

title: e2e-harness: harnessMailOverride() races on cold parallel auth requests, breaking the OTP read-back (onboarding-creator.spec.ts fails on main)
description:
PRE-EXISTING FAILURE ON MAIN, found by resonance-3f15 (Slice A step 6 e2e).

apps/web/lib/e2e-harness.ts harnessMailOverride() is not atomic:

  if (!store[HARNESS_MAIL_KEY]) {
    const { createFakeMail, observeLoginCodes } = await import("@resonance/auth/testing");
    const fake = createFakeMail();
    observeLoginCodes(fake);
    store[HARNESS_MAIL_KEY] = fake.port;
  }

There is an await between the guard and the assignment. The signup form fires TWO Better Auth
calls in parallel (signIn.magicLink + emailOtp.sendVerificationOtp, signup-form.tsx), so on a
cold dev server both requests pass the guard, both build a fake, and both call
observeLoginCodes(). One fake wins store[HARNESS_MAIL_KEY] (the port the auth instance actually
sends through); the other wins the process-wide observation slot registerObservedLoginCodes()
writes. peekLoginCode() then reads an array nothing ever pushes into, so
GET /api/test/last-otp returns {"otp":null} forever and the E2E cannot complete sign-in.

REPRO: pnpm --dir apps/web test:e2e -g "creator can sign up" on a cold server -> fails at the
OTP poll with 'Matcher error: received value must be a string'. A single direct POST to
/api/auth/email-otp/send-verification-otp works fine (no race). Issuing ONE warm auth request
(GET /api/auth/get-session) before the form makes it pass 3/3.

IMPACT: onboarding-creator.spec.ts 'creator can sign up, interview with Weave, generate + commit
a profile' is RED on main. apps/web/e2e/discovery.spec.ts carries a documented test-side warm-up
so the follow path can be verified; that warm-up should be deleted when this is fixed.

FIX: make the singleton construction race-free - build the fake synchronously behind a promise
pinned to globalThis (store the PROMISE, not the resolved port) so concurrent callers await the
same construction. Same shape applies to getWebAuth()'s store[HARNESS_AUTH_KEY] ??= createAuth(...).

Blast radius: apps/web/lib/e2e-harness.ts, apps/web/lib/auth.ts. Out of scope for resonance-3f15
(app source).

PROBLEM. apps/web/.env.local is gitignored, so a treehouse worktree never receives it. Every Slice A crewmate therefore built without the ability to boot the app against a real database, and six consecutive green pipelines (typecheck/lint/unit/build) said nothing about whether the feature worked. The step-6 crewmate was the first to run anything live and immediately found resonance-7912 (migration 0003 committed but unapplied; authenticated /discover 500s while anonymous is fine). Root cause is not the missing file — it is that 'gates green' was read as 'feature works'.

DECISION (jared, 2026-07-27). Do NOT copy the real apps/web/.env.local into worktrees. The disclosure risk is low (same user/machine; .gitignore line 17 uses the bare pattern '.env.local' so worktree copies are ignored too), but the CAPABILITY risk is real: up to max_trees=16 concurrent agents would hold live write access to the actual Neon database, a Resend key that sends real email, and API keys that spend real money. Instead give worktrees their OWN lower-privilege credentials so a confused agent's mistake is isolated and disposable.

DESIGN.
1. Per-worktree (or per-slice) Neon branch. Neon branching is cheap and copy-on-write. treehouse.toml post_create creates a branch off the dev database and writes its connection string as DATABASE_URL into the worktree's apps/web/.env.local; a matching pre-destroy/return hook deletes the branch. Agent DB mistakes then cannot touch shared dev data.
2. Sink email instead of the live Resend key. Either a Resend test-mode key or a dedicated sink address in VERIFY_LIVE_EMAIL_TO, so no agent can email a real person.
3. AI keys can be the real ones (they only cost tokens), or a separate lower-quota key if you want spend isolation.
4. Guard: the hook must assert the written .env.local is git-ignored in the target worktree and fail loudly if not — that is the one catastrophic path (an agent doing 'git add -f' then pushing).

BLOCKER. Cannot be implemented as-is today: there is no NEON_API_KEY in the environment and no neonctl on PATH, and the '.mcp.json' entry named 'neon' is actually @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres pointed at DATABASE_URL — a generic Postgres client that can query but CANNOT create or delete branches. Needs a Neon API key (or neonctl auth) before the post_create hook can be written.

INTERIM. Worktrees stay credential-less; any step needing live verification must say so and be run from the main checkout, or have .env.local copied in manually and deliberately for that one run (as was done for resonance-3f15).

RELATED: the schema-drift half of this problem is already fixed — scripts/verify-live.mjs now compares drizzle's journal against drizzle.__drizzle_migrations and names missing tags (commit 92eb0b8). Migrations are deliberately NOT auto-applied: drizzle-kit renders a rename as DROP COLUMN + ADD COLUMN, so applying unattended is silent data loss.

=== OPEN QUESTION, raised 2026-08-15, awaiting Jared: widen this to cover CI E2E? ===

As written above, this seed isolates TREEHOUSE WORKTREES. The question is whether to widen it so
CI E2E runs also get a per-run Neon branch.

WHAT WIDENING WOULD BUY:
  1. It would kill the fixture-leak class outright rather than mitigating it. Today every Playwright
     run writes into the SHARED dev database, so a spec that times out mid-teardown leaks rows that
     later runs then rank and count over. That is the mechanism behind resonance-1236 and the reason
     the cleanup backlog in resonance-4a2e exists. A per-run branch makes leaked rows disappear with
     the branch, so cleanup correctness stops being load-bearing.
  2. It would fix the gate's no-database problem. The no-mistakes gate cannot run a browser E2E in
     this repo and raises that as a finding on every run; browser evidence currently comes only from
     CI, which injects DATABASE_URL. A per-run branch is the missing piece that would let the gate
     itself exercise the real flow instead of deferring it.

COST AND UNKNOWNS, not yet investigated:
  - Still blocked on the same prerequisite as the rest of this seed: no NEON_API_KEY and no neonctl
     on PATH, and the .mcp.json entry named neon is a generic Postgres client that cannot create or
     delete branches.
  - Branch-per-run means create and delete on every CI run, not just on worktree lease and return.
     Needs a guaranteed teardown path so a cancelled or crashed run does not orphan branches, plus
     some idea of the Neon branch quota and what happens when it is hit.
  - Migrations must be applied to each fresh branch before the suite runs, and migrations are
     deliberately NOT auto-applied here (drizzle-kit renders a rename as DROP COLUMN + ADD COLUMN,
     which is silent data loss when run unattended). A fresh empty branch may make that safe, since
     there is no data to lose, but that reasoning needs checking rather than assuming.

DO NOT SCOPE THIS UP WITHOUT AN EXPLICIT ANSWER. It changes the seed from a local developer-ergonomics
task into CI infrastructure, and the two have different blast radii and different urgency.

title: e2e: Playwright drives pick-topics -> personalized /discover, and the skip path -> today's idle surface
description:
Drive the Slice B flow end to end in Playwright: sign up -> verify -> /interests -> pick topics -> personalized /discover, AND the skip path -> today's idle surface unchanged.

WIRING ALREADY IN PLACE (resonance-3a7d): /verify now lands on /interests for every new account; Continue there saves and continues to /onboarding/creator. Both existing specs were updated to click through the step by pressing Continue with nothing selected, so they assert the no-interests behaviour.

VERIFIED MANUALLY before this seed (throwaway spec, not committed): 13 chips render, picking 3 persists, and an empty-query /discover returns 20 ranked rows with the search box empty. So the feature works; this seed makes it a committed regression test.

GOTCHA FOUND, will cost you time otherwise: the chips are visually-hidden checkboxes inside their <label>, so 'getByRole("checkbox", {name}).check()' FAILS with 'label intercepts pointer events'. Drive it as a user does — 'getByText(label, {exact: true}).click()' — then assert 'toBeChecked()'. Not a user-facing bug (a real click lands on the label), purely a test-targeting issue.

ALSO: assert the skip path yields data-empty-state="idle" rather than 'no results' — 'nothing searched AND nothing to suggest' is a distinct surface from 'a query matched nothing', and collapsing them would blame the member for a query they never made. And beware seed resonance-1236: the discovery fixture query text is not run-scoped, so leaked rows can poison ranking assertions.

title: e2e: discovery fixture query text is not run-scoped, so leaked rows from any run poison the current one
description:
apps/web/e2e/lib/discovery-fixtures.ts scopes fixture DISPLAY NAMES per run (`E2E Top ${runId}`) but NOT the query text every run searches for. So every leaked `E2E Top` row from any past run embeds identically and scores similarity 1.0 against the current run's query, competing for the same 20-row first page.

OBSERVED 2026-07-29: a broken cleanup (the ::uuid cast in cleanup() after embeddings.source_id was widened to text) crashed the E2E *inside* cleanup, so each run leaked its 3 fixtures. 99 rows accumulated and filled /discover's first result page, pushing the current run's `E2E Second` off it. The failure surfaced as `expect(names).toContain(second)` — indistinguishable from a ranking regression in the freshly merged interest-ranking work, which is what made it expensive to diagnose. The code was correct; the corpus was poisoned.

The rows were cleared with Jared's approval (76 other users / 64 other profiles verified untouched), so the symptom is gone — but the fragility is not: any future cleanup failure reproduces it, and the test's own comment ('unrelated rows in the dev DB may legitimately sit between them') shows it was designed to tolerate unrelated rows, not near-identical siblings.

FIX: make the fixture query text run-scoped too, so leaked rows from other runs cannot score against the current query. Then a cleanup failure degrades to inert garbage instead of a cross-run test failure. Consider also asserting the fixture set is the ONLY thing matching its own query, so pollution fails loudly and locally rather than as a confusing ordering assertion.

title: web: /interests has no way to tell a member from a creator — decide the post-interests destination
description:
After Slice B, /interests sits between email verification and the rest of onboarding for EVERY newly verified account, and continues to /onboarding/creator — deliberately todays destination, unchanged. Members should arrive at /discover instead, but member and creator cannot be distinguished at that point.

ROOT CAUSE, and the reason this is not really a routing problem: setUserRoles is NEVER called from app code. The Better Auth roles column defaults to "member" and nothing ever writes "creator", so the app has no notion of who is a creator. Verified by grep: only build artifacts reference it.

DESIGN CONTEXT: the design supports BOTH entry paths — /start (Onboarding/Creator/WhatBroughtYou 1519:78312) forks on intent, AND Member/TurntoCreator (1443:78478, 2 variants) exists as a member-to-creator conversion screen.

OPTIONS (Jared is second-guessing the current answer; not yet decided):

1. EVERYONE goes to /discover; creator onboarding becomes a deliberate act via the TurnToCreator path. Design-truest and smallest change. Cost: the /start creator intent gets weaker, and onboarding-creator.spec.ts must navigate rather than land.

2. MAKE CREATOR-HOOD REAL DATA and route on the role. /start intent carried to signup, which writes roles = member,creator; /interests then routes on session.roles. NOTE this is materially different from the next-URL threading already declined: that was a transient redirect target with an open-redirect surface needing an allowlist, this is a closed enum that becomes durable data useful beyond routing (creator-only surfaces, the TurnToCreator conversion, analytics). Biggest change — touches signup and auth.

3. Intent in an httpOnly cookie set at /start, read once at /interests. No URL param, no redirect surface, but invisible in the data model and solves only routing — the same gap returns the first time anything else needs the distinction.

4. Two routes, one component: /interests (member, goes to /discover) plus the creator flow rendering the same picker at its own step (goes to /onboarding/creator). No runtime fork; the route encodes the destination. Cost: two entry points to keep in sync.

RULED OUT: adding a where-next control to the interests screen — the frame does not draw one and ADR-0019 forbids inventing UI.

1 and 2 are combinable: do 1 now, do 2 when creator-hood needs to be real.

Blast radius for any option: apps/web/app/(onboarding)/interests/actions.ts (AFTER_INTERESTS), verify-form.tsx and signup-form.tsx (AFTER_VERIFY must stay identical in both or the channel used changes the destination), and both E2E specs which currently click through /interests by submitting an empty selection.
=== DECIDED 2026-08-09: OPTION 2 — make creator-hood real data ===

Jared chose option 2: carry the /start intent through signup, write roles = member,creator, and route /interests on session.roles. Reason it beat option 1: a closed enum that becomes durable data is useful beyond routing (creator-only surfaces, the TurnToCreator conversion, analytics), whereas option 1 only moves the destination. Options 3 and 4 are not being pursued.

BLAST RADIUS — REVISED, the note above is now stale. The Slice B e2e refactor shrank it:

  apps/web/app/(onboarding)/signup/signup-form.tsx     AFTER_VERIFY = "/interests"
  apps/web/app/(onboarding)/verify/verify-form.tsx     AFTER_VERIFY = "/interests"  (SAME value in both, on purpose — the magic-link and OTP channels must not diverge, or which channel a member used would change where they land)
  apps/web/app/(onboarding)/interests/actions.ts       AFTER_INTERESTS = "/onboarding/creator"  ← the routing fork goes here
  apps/web/e2e/lib/signup.ts                           AFTER_INTERESTS regex + skipInterests() — ONE place now, not three

The three E2E specs no longer hand-roll the interests click; they all go through signUpAndVerify() and skipInterests() in e2e/lib/signup.ts, so the expected post-interests destination is a single constant. That was done deliberately to confine this seed.

STILL TO DESIGN, and the real work of this seed — the option list does not answer it:
  1. HOW the intent survives signup. Better Auth's magic-link callbackURL is the only thing currently threaded through, and a next-URL param was already declined for its open-redirect surface. A closed enum in the callback path, a signed cookie, or a pre-signup row are all candidates.
  2. WHERE roles get written. setUserRoles exists in @resonance/db and is currently called ONLY by commitCreatorProfile (which appends "creator" at profile commit). Writing "creator" earlier, at signup, means two writers for the same column — decide whether commit stays additive-idempotent or becomes a no-op.
  3. Whether an existing member converting via Member/TurnToCreator (Figma 1443:78478) uses the same write path.

VERIFY WITH: both E2E specs plus a new assertion that a member intent lands on /discover and a creator intent lands on /onboarding/creator. Note the E2E harness fakes mail, so the magic-link channel is drivable end to end.

=== SUPERSEDED 2026-08-14: the decision above is STALE. Read this instead. ===

The DECIDED-2026-08-09 block says roles = member,creator written at signup, routed on session.roles. That is NOT what is being built, and implementing it would be wrong.

WHY IT CHANGED. Reading the code during planning surfaced a collision the option list never mentioned: commitCreatorProfile (packages/ai/src/agents/profile-gen/commit-profile.ts) writes the role LAST on purpose and documents the invariant - a member only becomes a creator once a discoverable profile+embedding is durably persisted. Writing creator at signup contradicts that. It would have been invisible, because NOTHING in the repo reads roles for authorization: the only reader is commitCreatorProfile reading currentRoles to append to, and /discover gates on the creator_profiles row, not the role.

Jared then ruled on review that a not-yet state does not belong in the role enum at all - being a creator implies having gone THROUGH creator onboarding.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BEING BUILT (plan pl-1b6e, revision 5, approved):
  - RoleSchema is UNCHANGED. @resonance/ai is UNTOUCHED.
  - The intent gets its own home: OnboardingIntentSchema in @resonance/core (explore|share|business) plus a new NULLABLE user.onboarding_intent column with no default.
  - /start intent travels as a closed enum in the URL through BOTH verify channels, is Zod-parsed at /interests, persisted via setOnboardingIntent in @resonance/db, and forks the destination there.
  - Two further reasons this beat the creator_pending variant: a single pending role collapses share vs business, which the design forks on and analytics wants; and decodeRoles calls RoleSchema.parse and THROWS on unrecognized values, so widening the role enum created a rollback hazard a separate column does not.

STATUS: step 1 (core, resonance-bc02) is DONE and closed - PR #27, awaiting merge. resonance-cdc2 (the ai step) was closed as OBSOLETE. Remaining: ab47 (ui), 0084 (db), 52d8 (web), 9719 (e2e). Full approach, alternatives, risks and acceptance live in sd plan show pl-1b6e.

title: Repo-wide sweep: remove session/procedural references from code comments
description:
Ratified 2026-08-09, codified in docs/conventions.md (Comments) and CLAUDE.md golden rule 11: a code comment describes the code, never the process that produced it. Session and procedural references are out; ADR-00xx and Figma node ids stay, because they are durable, checked into the repo, and about the product rather than the session.

OUT of comments: seed ids (resonance-xxxx), plan ids (pl-xxxx), mulch ids (mx-xxxxxx), "Slice A/B/C", "Increment N", "golden rule N", "plan risk N", "acceptance criterion N", "this slice"/"the slice"/"this seed", and pointers to CLAUDE.md or conventions.md.

IN: plain-English rationale, ADR-00xx citations, Figma node ids. Citations follow the reason rather than replacing it, so the comment stands alone for a reader who never opens docs/.

WHY: a reader who was not in the session cannot resolve any of it. "golden rule 4" names nothing they can see.

REMAINING AFTER THE SLICE B SWEEP, measured on main at 8395e3c across apps/ and packages/, excluding dist/:

title: e2e-harness.test.ts beforeAll flakes on the 10s hook timeout under parallel test load
description:
apps/web/lib/e2e-harness.test.ts intermittently fails its beforeAll with "Hook timed out in 10000ms" when the whole monorepo suite runs in parallel via pnpm test. All 4 tests in the file then report as SKIPPED and the web test task exits 1, which fails the run and cascades ELIFECYCLE noise from the other packages as turbo cancels them.

EVIDENCE, observed 2026-08-09 on an unrelated comment-only branch: run 1 failed, runs 2 and 3 passed, on IDENTICAL code. Standalone (pnpm --filter web test) it passes every time and the file takes about 750ms; under full parallel load the same hook exceeds 10s. It is load, not logic.

CAUSE: the beforeAll calls vi.stubEnv + vi.resetModules and then dynamically re-imports the harness module twice (once with E2E_HARNESS on, once off). Under CPU contention from the other 15 turbo tasks, that module graph re-resolution blows past vitest's 10s default hookTimeout.

FIX, with precedent already in this repo: raise the hook timeout for this file rather than the whole suite. packages/db/src/queries/discovery.test.ts and interests.test.ts already do exactly this for the same reason - their comments say the PGlite work exceeds the 10s default under parallel test-suite CPU contention in CI. Match that approach, and state the reason in the comment in plain English per the comment convention.

WHY IT MATTERS: this fails CI non-deterministically on changes that have nothing to do with it, which trains people to re-run rather than read a red build. It also cost time on the comment-convention change, where it had to be ruled out as a regression before that work could ship.

NOT a regression from any recent change - the file is untouched by the branches where it surfaced.

title: web/ui: Member/TurnToCreator conversion screen (Figma 1443:78478) calls setOnboardingIntent
analytics: setOnboardingIntent overwrites, so the member-to-creator CONVERSION signal is never recorded
description:
setOnboardingIntent writes the latest stated intent, overwriting any earlier one. That is the right behaviour for what the column is scoped to (routing and conversion) and it is safe because intent is not status, so an overwrite can never demote anyone. But it means the column answers only "what do they say now", never "what did they say first, and did that change".

WHAT IS LOST. Someone who answers explore at /start, browses as a member, and later converts through Member/TurnToCreator ends up with onboarding_intent = share. The fact that they ARRIVED as an explorer and CONVERTED is gone. That transition is arguably the most valuable signal the whole intent design produces: it is the member-to-creator funnel, and it was one of the reasons cited for making creator-hood real data rather than a transient redirect.

WHY IT WAS NOT SOLVED IN PLAN pl-1b6e. A single text column physically cannot hold a history. Capturing the transition needs an append-only row per statement (user id, intent, stated-at, and where it was stated: signup versus conversion screen), which is a different shape from the current column and was out of scope for the decided work. Raised during Wave 2 review and deliberately deferred rather than silently accepted.

OPTIONS, none evaluated yet:
1. An onboarding_intent_events table, append-only. The user column stays as the fast current-value read; the table carries the history. Most faithful, most work.
2. Keep only the FIRST intent in a second column (onboarding_intent_initial) alongside the current one. Cheap, captures arrival-versus-now, but collapses any path with more than two statements.
3. Emit to an analytics sink rather than storing it, if one ever exists. No schema change, but nothing queryable from the app.

DEPENDS ON whether the funnel is actually a question anyone will ask. If conversion rate is never measured, doing nothing is correct and this seed should be closed rather than built. Jared to decide.

GROWS FROM HERE. Step 5 of plan pl-1b6e adds an intent variant to the E2E specs, which means MORE accounts created per run, not fewer. The backlog will grow faster than it did before.

title: e2e: the account-signing specs exceed Playwright's default 30s budget, and only CI retries hide it
description:
Measured on 2026-09-01 against the real Neon DB. Every spec that drives the passwordless front door (discovery follow, interests x2, onboarding-creator) fails on a cold server and passes on a warm one, because the work genuinely straddles the default 30s per-test budget:

- first test to touch a route: ~23s (next dev compiles it) vs ~3s for the same test warm
- five workers against a cold server: ~33s each
- full suite serial + warm: all 15 pass, slowest 18.8s

Reproduced on main with none of the intent work applied: 3 of 10 failed cold/parallel, the same account-signing specs, so this is not a regression from the signup helper refactor.

CI does not fail because retries: 2 means attempt two runs warm. That makes a green CI run evidence that the SECOND attempt passed, not that the flow works — and it is why this has stayed invisible.

onboarding-intent.spec.ts already sets its own 90s budget (test.describe.configure). The fix is to decide the home for that: either the same per-file budget on each account-signing spec, or a global timeout in playwright.config.ts, which is arguably the honest place since the cost comes from next dev being the E2E server rather than from any one spec.

Worth pairing with a look at teardown: one discovery.spec.ts account leaked during a timed-out parallel run and had to be deleted by hand (cleaned up 2026-09-01). Adjacent to resonance-4a2e (dev DB backlog) and resonance-1236 (fixture run-scoping).

title: infra: the no-mistakes gate worktree has no DATABASE_URL, so it cannot run the Playwright specs
description:
The gate clones into ~/.no-mistakes/repos/<id>.git and works from that checkout. DATABASE_URL lives only in the repo-root .env, which is gitignored (.gitignore:16, along with .env.local and .env.*.local), so it never reaches the worktree — and it is not in the OS environment either (the pipeline agent checked process env plus Windows User and Machine scopes). Creating apps/web/.env.local in the main working copy does not help for the same reason.

Consequence, seen on run 01M1FPGNVJYG5MKDH51768NYMD: the test step parked an ask-user finding saying the change's central claim could not be demonstrated, because all five onboarding-intent specs sign real accounts up against Neon. It verified everything provable without a database (unit tests, the new route's live 200/400/404 surface, the intent carried through real browser URLs, the hook fix as a before/after regression) and reported the rest as a warning. The specs were proven green locally instead — 15/15, cold and fully parallel — which is evidence outside the gate rather than in it.

Fix: make DATABASE_URL visible to the daemon so every process it spawns inherits it, the way CI does with secrets.DATABASE_URL. Either start the daemon from a shell that exports it (process-scoped, nothing written to disk) or persist it in the Windows User scope (automatic for every future run, but readable by any process running as that user, and every gate run then creates and deletes real accounts in the shared dev DB). Decide which tradeoff is wanted.

Related: gh CLI is not authenticated, so the same run skipped both the pr and ci steps ('skipping PR creation: gh CLI is not authenticated'). Worth fixing together, since neither gap is about the code being gated.
